primary_claim: Bias-augmented Consistency Training (BCT) and a newly introduced Activation Consistency Training (ACT) both increase robustness to sycophancy-inducing and jailbreak-wrapper cues relative to baselines across Gemma 2/3 and Gemini 2.5 Flash, with BCT reducing Gemini 2.5 Flash's attack success rate on ClearHarm from 67.8% to 2.9%.

effect.metric: Attack Success Rate (ASR) on ClearHarm, BCT vs. baseline (Gemini 2.5 Flash)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Builds on Bias-augmented Consistency Training from Chua et al. (2025), extending it with a new activation-level variant (ACT)
The stale-data SFT baseline performed strictly worse than BCT, evidence that stale training data from older/weaker models can damage the capabilities of newer models being finetuned on it
limitations_stated: A third baseline, Negative Preference Optimization (NPO), could not be tuned to work well on their benchmarks despite strong performance in prior work, so it was excluded from the results
ACT reduced jailbreaks less effectively than BCT, though it rarely made the model more likely to refuse benign prompts
Stale-data SFT experiments were not run for Gemma 2
quote: BCT reduced the attack success rate on ClearHarm from 67.8% down to 2.9%.
